SAS DATDIF(sdate, edate, basis)

Source: R/doc_functions.R
sas_f_datdif.Rd

Days between two dates under a day-count basis. See the SAS documentation (Functions and CALL Routines).

Arguments

start

Starting SAS date value (SAS sdate). Missing gives missing.

end

Ending SAS date value (SAS edate); before start gives a negative result. Missing gives missing.

basis

Day-count basis: 'ACT/ACT' (or 'ACTUAL') counts actual days; '30/360' (or '360') counts 30-day months, treating the 31st as the 30th. Default 'ACT/ACT'.

Value

A vector with one result per element (arguments are recycled), as the SAS function returns per observation.

Differences from R

SAS dates count days and SAS datetimes count seconds from 1960-01-01; R's Date and POSIXct start at 1970-01-01.

See also

Other datetime functions: sas_f_date(), sas_f_datejul(), sas_f_datepart(), sas_f_datetime(), sas_f_day(), sas_f_dhms(), sas_f_hms(), sas_f_hour(), sas_f_intck(), sas_f_intnx(), sas_f_juldate(), sas_f_juldate7(), sas_f_mdy(), sas_f_minute(), sas_f_month(), sas_f_qtr(), sas_f_second(), sas_f_time(), sas_f_timepart(), sas_f_today(), sas_f_week(), sas_f_weekday(), sas_f_year(), sas_f_yrdif()

Examples

# DATDIF: each call is explained above it and followed by its result
# (SAS dates are day counts from 1960-01-01; datetimes and times are seconds)

# With basis 'ACT/ACT' DATDIF counts actual days: 31 in January plus 29 in
# February 2024 = 60.
sas_f_datdif(23376, 23436, "ACT/ACT")  # datdif('01JAN2024'd, '01MAR2024'd, 'ACT/ACT') = 60
#> [1] 60

# Basis '30/360' treats every month as 30 days, so two months are 60 days.
sas_f_datdif(23376, 23436, "30/360")  # datdif('01JAN2024'd, '01MAR2024'd, '30/360') = 60
#> [1] 60

# Under '30/360' the 31st counts as the 30th, so 31 January to 1 March is 31
# days.
sas_f_datdif(23406, 23436, "30/360")  # datdif('31JAN2024'd, '01MAR2024'd, '30/360') = 31
#> [1] 31

# If the end date is before the start date, the result is negative.
sas_f_datdif(23436, 23376, "ACT/ACT")  # datdif('01MAR2024'd, '01JAN2024'd, 'ACT/ACT') = -60
#> [1] -60
